checklist.notes: The language and task demands in the A1-U02-L02 WRITING AI-practice prompt are broadly appropriate for its declared CEFR tier.
No material English grammar, lexical, pronunciation-description, or meaning error was found in the reviewed A1-U02-L02 WRITING AI-practice prompt.
The request-only model does not communicate the rubric’s required run sense or present/past contrast.
The draft-first and bounded-feedback states are coherent, but the learner-visible task cannot reliably elicit every hidden rubric target.
The example sentence is natural in isolation; the problem is its mismatch with the unstated assessment requirements.

No suspiciously distinctive copied passage is apparent in the short A1-U02-L02 WRITING AI-practice prompt, but internal inspection cannot establish originality beyond the retained project evidence and no Internet-wide comparison was performed.

findings.description: The request-only model does not communicate the rubric’s required run sense or present/past contrast.
findings.recommendation: Tell learners explicitly to write one authorized request and one sentence or pair showing the specified run and tense contrast.

limitations: This review covers only the immutable A1-U02-L02 WRITING AI-practice prompt and its fresh static machine-report context. It does not assess human or release approval, provider authentication, live-provider behavior, learner outcomes, or Internet-wide originality.
